reuse.why: Reuses d.isWeekend and the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend path, but does not extend getDateWithSkippedWeekend or getNextDate into a shared weekend-rule definition; getUpcomingDates re-implements the daily skip instead of going through getNextDate.

duplication.why: The 'skipWeekend && frequency === daily' predicate, the widened take and the isWeekend filter are written separately in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate and server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates.

placement.why: Storing frequency in the rschedule data in parseRecurDate is sensible, but the rule is spread across a shared util and a server handler rather than living next to getDateWithSkippedWeekend.

scope.why: Only the files needed for the daily-weekend rule are touched.

maintainability.why: The weekend rule now exists in two hand-written variants, and the schedule-template budget path (which calls getNextDate with noSkipWeekend and moves weekends itself) was not updated, so the rule is inconsistent across paths.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates filters weekend occurrences inline instead of using a shared weekend-rule function; server/budget/schedule-template.ts still applies getDateWithSkippedWeekend directly to daily schedules.

disguised_duplication.where: skipsDailyWeekends predicate + take-widening + isWeekend filter appear in getNextDate (as a firstWeekday closure, take 7) and in getUpcomingDates (inline filter, take count*7), reshaped rather than shared.

one_place.where: The daily-skip rule is implemented separately in shared/schedules.ts getNextDate and server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates, and server/budget/schedule-template.ts still moves weekend dates of daily schedules via getDateWithSkippedWeekend.
